source.title: Analyzing & Reducing the Need for Learning Rate Warmup in GPT Training
source.authors: Atli Kosson; Bettina Messmer; Martin Jaggi

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper and appendices; no obvious cutoff or garbling affects the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports controlled warmup and optimizer-modification results that refine when large-batch training benefits from warmup, including conditions where the penalty is reduced or eliminated. It does not test the listed natural-label generalization, memorization, width, optimizer-comparison, or sharpness claims directly.
record.gate_note: The paper studies GPT training stability and validation loss under warmup, not train-test generalization gaps or fitting arbitrary labels. Rows below capture only results directly relevant to V5's large-batch/warmup condition: batch size 480 and 124M GPT2 baseline, Lion optimizer variants, and the paper's model and dataset ablations. Figure-only values are recorded as figure only; cited prior work is excluded.
record.test_reason: The study measures warmup effects and optimizer modifications at a fixed batch size, rather than the held-out performance difference between large and small batches under equal epoch budgets. Removing a warmup/no-warmup gap does not demonstrate removal of V5's large/small-batch penalty. Its critical-batch-size analysis concerns representation changes and optimization, without testing any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that warmup limits effective early updates; controlling update norms or angles alone does not always suffice. Representation-change compensation and higher momentum combined with angular control can reduce or eliminate warmup dependence in tested settings. They recommend short warmup pending broader validation.
record.recipe_differences: This paper studies warmup and optimizer modifications in small-scale GPT language-model training, measuring validation loss and update/representation changes. It does not use the claim's random-label memorization/generalization recipe or the specified image-classification comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Warmup benefit varies with optimizer modification (ℓ2 versus angular update control, RRC compensation, momentum), dataset (OpenWebText versus SlimPajama), and architecture (GPT2 versus Llama2).

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed batch size 480, warmup improves baseline GPT2 validation loss. Update-norm control retains this benefit; angular control reduces it; representation-change compensation or higher-momentum corrected LionAR can eliminate it. Results depend on architecture and dataset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Warmup dependence in small language-model training can be reduced or eliminated by modifying effective early updates, with outcomes depending on optimizer and architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: The representation-change derivation predicts stronger learning-rate downscaling at high gradient signal-to-noise ratios and larger batches. Measured signal-to-noise ratios are high initially, but batch size is not experimentally varied.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High initial gradient alignment can amplify representation changes from normalized updates and motivate warmup, especially at larger batch sizes.

record.problems: The main experiments focus on a single 124M GPT2 model, one batch size, and a limited hyperparameter range. The authors do not quantify uncertainty for every configuration; they report run-to-run validation-loss differences around 0.05 for selected baseline runs. They state that broader validation is needed for the warmup-reduction methods.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant rows omitted. The paper's ResNet-20 experiments examine large initial updates, dead ReLUs, and final test accuracy, but do not test the listed large-batch fixed-epoch claim or another mapped version, so they are excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label held-out generalization.
Test-error changes when widening beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization under limited or broader tuning; no such optimizer comparison is reported.
Large versus small batches under equal epoch budgets, and whether recipe adaptations shrink that performance difference. Warmup is varied only at a fixed batch size.
Dropout effects, small-data exceptions, excessive dropout, and joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness ranking generalization gaps against other measures. Angular update size and representation change are different quantities.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The corrected states describe whether rows establish a listed version, not whether their reported warmup effects exist. No listed version warrants a verdict. The original V5 labels conflate a warmup/no-warmup gap with a large/small-batch gap.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error after widening beyond interpolation.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.

The paper does not compare large and small batches under fixed epoch budgets; its central GPT experiments use batch size 480 and vary warmup and optimizer setup. It does not evaluate the language-model batch-size penalty as a function of batch size.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of generalization gaps.

rows.subject: GPT2-124M
rows.operation_detail: Baseline AdamW training with warmup percentages swept; learning rate and warmup length swept, with 50% linear cooldown.
rows.baseline: Best no-warmup run; exact numeric loss not stated in text
rows.value: Short warmup significantly improves performance; no-warmup has a performance gap. Figure 1 shows values only.
rows.uncertainty: not stated for each configuration; baseline run-to-run validation-loss differences around 0.05 over seeds
rows.note: The paper states the qualitative result in text and presents plotted loss values; exact point values are figure only.
rows.check: Warmup versus no warmup at batch size 480 measures a schedule effect, not V5's batch-size penalty.

rows.subject: GPT2-124M
rows.operation_detail: LionA training sweep controls the ℓ2 update norm while varying warmup.
rows.baseline: No-warmup LionA run; exact numeric loss not stated in text
rows.value: Warmup advantage remains despite perfect control of the ℓ2 update norm; exact plotted losses not stated in text.
rows.note: The text explicitly says the benefit of warmup remains and the no-warmup penalty remains significant.
rows.check: The retained warmup advantage under update-norm control does not measure a large/small-batch performance difference.

rows.subject: GPT2-124M
rows.operation_detail: LionAR rotational optimizer controls angular update size while varying warmup.
rows.baseline: No-warmup LionAR run; exact numeric loss not stated in text
rows.value: Controlling angular updates reduces, but does not fully eliminate, the benefit of warmup.
rows.note: The text describes a reduced but still significant no-warmup performance gap.
rows.check: Angular control reduces the warmup advantage; no batch-size comparison establishes a partial V5 effect.

rows.subject: GPT2-124M
rows.operation_detail: LionAR with relative representation change correction while varying warmup.
rows.baseline: No-warmup run; exact numeric loss not stated in text
rows.value: Correction helps close the warmup/no-warmup gap, but overall performance is slightly worse; it does not benefit from warmup in the plotted sweep.
rows.note: Text says the correction acts like automatic warmup and helps close the gap; it also notes the overall performance is slightly worse and the setting has practical limitations.
rows.check: Closing the warmup gap does not establish closing a batch-size penalty. The condition also includes weight decay increased by 32 times, without tuning that factor.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT2-124M on OpenWebText at batch size 480 with baseline AdamW, LionA, or LionAR
reader_labels.reason: Short warmup improves validation loss; ℓ2 control leaves the gap, while angular control reduces but does not eliminate it (R1–R3). The paper does not sweep batch size, so this is evidence about warmup at one large batch setting, not a direct large-versus-small batch comparison.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT2-124M on OpenWebText at batch size 480 with RRC correction or higher-momentum corrected LionAR
reader_labels.reason: The RRC correction and higher-momentum corrected LionAR remove the observed warmup benefit in the plotted setting (R4, R5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Dataset and architecture ablations: SlimPajama GPT2 and OpenWebText Llama2
reader_labels.reason: The warmup gap depends on optimizer, dataset, and architecture: LionA still benefits on SlimPajama, while LionAR eliminates the need on Llama2 models (R7–R14).
